In a Unique Factorization Domain (UFD) R[x], a polynomial f(x) is primitive if its greatest common divisor (GCD) with any other polynomial in R[x] is 1. This means that f(x) cannot be factored into the product of two non-constant polynomials in R[x].

Now, let f(x) and g(x) be two primitive polynomials in R[x]. We need to show that their product f(x)g(x) is also primitive.

Now, since f(x) and g(x) are coprime, their GCD is 1. This implies that c = 1, since c divides both f(x) and g(x). Therefore, h(x) = 1, which contradicts the assumption that h(x) divides both f(x) and g(x).

Hence, we conclude that the product f(x)g(x) is primitive.

Let f(x) and g(x) be two coprime polynomials in R[x]. We need to show that their GCD in F[x] is 1.

Since f(x) and g(x) are coprime in R[x], their GCD in R[x] is 1. Now, consider the field of fractions F[x] of R[x]. Any element in F[x] can be written as a fraction p(x)/q(x), where p(x) and q(x) are polynomials in R[x].

Since f(x) and g(x) are coprime in R[x], their GCD in R[x] is 1. Therefore, the GCD of u(x)f(x) and v(x)g(x) is 1.
